assertions.name: imq_small_and_sign_flipped
assertions.source: required Im(q)=eps from S: small (<10% Re q) AND sign-flipped mu/p — candidate (iii) signature

description: Tests conj:im-q-physical-role candidate (iii) (Im(q) = non-Hermitian / decay-width Γ parameter) against the c₃ bar-odd S = Q_β/E₀, the decay observable it predicted. Non-fitting inversion: S as the first-order response of Im 𝔙 to Im(q)=ε, with the derived meridian map u=2 log q (#3579) and leading NZ Im 𝔙 ≈ (√3/2)|u|²sin(2 arg u). Required ε: muon +1.3%, proton −5.5% of Re q — small-ish and SIGN-FLIPPED. Real q₀ differ ~1e-8, so ε is an independent DOF; the sign-flip (impossible for real q) is the candidate-(iii) signature. Does NOT close the wall (the q₀↦ε map = arg(u(q₀)) stays open, now read as the decay projection). No conflict with Im q₀=0 (that is the bar-even mass eval; S is ∂/∂Im q). Magnitude u-map-dependent; sign-flip robust. Scope-(a); C14; no fit; no c_k wired; conjecture stays a conjecture.

derivation.u_map: u = 2 log q (meridian holonomy = mult by q, #3579)
derivation.im_V_leading: (sqrt3/2)|u|^2 sin(2 arg u), sqrt3 = derived cusp shape tau=2 sqrt(-3)
derivation.response: S ≈ (4 sqrt3 log q0 / q0) eps

interpretation.sign_flip: eps(muon)>0>eps(proton): imaginary DOF carries the sign-flip real q cannot
interpretation.no_im_q0_conflict: masses = value at Im q=0 (lusztig_q_0_imaginary_part_zero); S = d/d(Im q) response
interpretation.magnitude_caveat: |eps| depends on the u-map; sign-flip is robust (=sign S)
